subtitle: Lesson 21 · Working With GPUs in PyTorch

eyebrow: Hundreds of tiny launches add up

steps.label: Dispatch
steps.sub: hands it to the GPU's command queue

steps.label: Repeat
steps.sub: once per kernel, however small the work

code:
g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    static_y = model(static_input)
    static_loss = loss_fn(static_y, static_target)
    static_loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
caption: Warm-up runs happen in a side stream first — PyTorch requires it before capture

eyebrow: Replay: one CPU dispatch for the whole sequence
code:
for data, target in loader:
    static_input.copy_(data)     # copy INTO the static tensor
    static_target.copy_(target)
    g.replay()
caption: Shape, dtype, and memory address must stay fixed across every replay
